In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the non-invasive presurgery diagnostic protocol for temporal lop epilepsy is feasible and effective.
the non-invasive presurgery protocol is a safe, effective, and efficient method of selecting patients with TLE for surgery.

the use of the proposed presurgical protocol in the present study allowed the identification of three different TLE subsyn-dromes, which could be treated effectively and with low surgical risks by means of tailored surgical strategies, thus improving the outcome of TLE surgery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-invasive protocol is useful for TLE surgery, and that different surgical approaches can be used for different TLE subsndromes.
a non-invasive protocol based on anatomo–clinical–electro correlations can be successfully applied for TLE surgery.
the “anatomo-electro-clinical” approach can identify different TLE subtypes and can guide the surgical approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when possible, a non-invasive protocol should be used for patients with temporal lobe epilepsy, as the risk/benefit ratio is better for the patients.
a non-invasive protocol can be successfully used in TLE patients with a short duration of seizure history, and that the surgical strategy should be tailored to the specific type of TLE.

, in TLE patients with a history of seizures of <2 years, an MRI with concordant clinical and EEG findings is sufficient to allow for the diagnosis of TLE, and for the identification of a specific TLE syndrome.
